title: Overnight Blueberry Oats with Almond-Seed Topping
description: Rolled oats, chia and coconut soaked overnight with banana and blueberries, then finished in the morning with a crunchy almond, flaxseed and sunflower topping. No cooking and no pastry despite the original name.
keeps_note: Made the night before and eaten cold; holds 2 to 3 days.

ingredients.estimate_basis: a quarter lemon yields about 3/4 tablespoon

instructions.text: Combine the oats, chia seeds, 2 tablespoons of the coconut flakes, and 1/2 teaspoon of the cinnamon in a mixing bowl.
Put the banana pieces into a small bowl. Sprinkle with the lemon juice and stir in 1 tablespoon of the agave nectar, making sure each piece of banana is coated.

Stir the bananas, half the blueberries, and the coconut milk into the oat mixture and combine. Spoon evenly into two serving bowls, pressing the banana pieces into the oats. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Meanwhile, make the topping. In a small bowl, stir the almonds, flaxseed, and sunflower seeds together. Stir in the remaining cinnamon and agave nectar. Cover and let stand until morning.
Before serving, sprinkle the topping over the oats and decorate with the remaining coconut flakes and blueberries.

notes: Needs to soak overnight, so start it the evening before. The oats can also be warmed gently before the topping goes on.
household_edits: Raw honey swapped for raw agave nectar so the recipe is vegan.
Renamed from "Blueberry and Oats Pie" — there is no pastry and it is not baked.

title: Acai and Berry Breakfast Jar
description: A layered breakfast jar of strawberries, raspberries and blueberries blended with homemade raw coconut yogurt, chia and acai, chilled overnight and topped with cashew butter, hemp seeds and mint. Includes the coconut yogurt recipe, which makes more than the jar needs.
keeps_note: Chills overnight in the jar; the spare coconut yogurt keeps a week.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 cup frozen raw white coconut meat (about 8 ounces), thawed and coarsely chopped
ingredients.prep_note: thawed if frozen, coarsely chopped; or the white meat of 1/2 fresh coconut

instructions.text: Make the coconut yogurt. Blend the coconut meat and coconut water until smooth. Empty the powder from the probiotic capsule into the mixture and blend again for a few seconds.

Pour the coconut mixture into a bowl, cover, and let stand overnight at warm room temperature. In the morning you should have about 1 1/4 cups of yogurt. Take what you need; the rest keeps in the refrigerator for up to a week.

Blend 1/2 cup of the strawberries, 2/3 cup of the raspberries, and 3 tablespoons of the blueberries with the yogurt, coconut milk, vanilla seeds, chia seeds, agave nectar, acai powder, and lemon juice until smooth. Pour into a wide-necked jar of 10 to 12 ounce capacity. Cover and chill overnight.
The following morning, top with the cashew butter and the remaining berries, followed by the hemp seeds and mint sprigs.

notes: The coconut yogurt ferments overnight at room temperature, and the jar then chills overnight, so allow two evenings or make the yogurt in advance. It makes about 1 1/4 cups — roughly twice what this jar needs.
household_edits: Raw honey swapped for raw agave nectar so the recipe is vegan.

title: Buckwheat Breakfast Bowl
description: Sprouted raw buckwheat served with coconut yogurt, orange zest and juice, goji berries, raspberries, apple, pomegranate and passion fruit, warmed through with cinnamon and turmeric. The buckwheat needs three days of planning but almost no work.
keeps_note: Sprout the buckwheat ahead; assembled bowls are best the same day.

ingredients.raw_text: grated zest and juice of 1 orange
1 Granny Smith apple, cored and diced

ingredients.estimate_basis: one pomegranate yields about 1 cup of seeds

instructions.text: Rinse the buckwheat three times in fresh water to clean it. Put it into a bowl with the cold water and soak for 20 minutes.

Drain and rinse the buckwheat, then let it stand at room temperature — in either a sprouting tray or a strainer set over a bowl — for 36 hours. Rinse the buckwheat if it looks sticky, then again before using.
Rinse, drain, and divide the buckwheat among four bowls. Divide the yogurt among the bowls, sprinkle with the remaining ingredients, and serve.

notes: The buckwheat sprouts for 36 hours, so start two days ahead. Sprouted buckwheat is not recommended for young children, older adults, pregnant women, or anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Pear, Banana, and Apple Breakfast Bowl
original_title: Pear, Banana, and Apple Breakfast Bowl
description: Chopped pear, apple and banana in a lightly spiced blended fruit puree, finished with cashews, sunflower seeds, golden raisins, goldenberries and dried cranberries. Nothing is cooked and it comes together in about ten minutes.
keeps_note: The apple and banana darken within a few hours — make it the morning you want it.

ingredients.raw_text: 2 ripe dessert pears, such as Bartlett
2 green-skinned apples, such as Granny Smith

ingredients.estimate_basis: half a lemon yields about 1 1/2 tablespoons

instructions.text: Core and chop one pear and one apple. Put them into a serving bowl with half the banana and pour over half the apple juice and half the lemon juice. Stir well to combine.
Core, peel, and coarsely chop the remaining pear and apple. Add them to a blender with the rest of the banana.
Add the remaining apple juice and lemon juice to the blender with the golden raisins and nuts. Blend until you have a finely chopped mixture.

Stir the blended mixture into the chopped fruit, along with the sunflower seeds, sugar, and cinnamon. Sprinkle with the goldenberries and cranberries. Chill in the refrigerator if you have time, or serve immediately.

notes: Goldenberries are dried ground cherries, also sold as husk tomatoes — small, tangy orange fruits wrapped in a papery husk.

title: Berry Overnight Oats
description: A single jar of rolled oats soaked overnight in almond milk with flaxseed, acai powder and goji berries, topped in the morning with blueberries, strawberries and slivered almonds. Made in the jar you carry it to work in.
keeps_note: Built the night before in a sealed jar; holds 2 to 3 days.

instructions.text: Put the oats, flaxseed, acai berry powder, goji berries, most of the slivered almonds, the agave nectar, and almond milk into an 8-ounce jar with a lid. Stir well.
Stir a few of the blueberries into the oat mixture. Secure the lid on the jar and chill in the refrigerator overnight.
In the morning, chop the strawberries. Top the oats with the remaining blueberries, strawberries, and the remaining almonds.

notes: Soaks overnight. Scales cleanly — make several jars at once for the week.
household_edits: Raw honey swapped for raw agave nectar so the recipe is vegan.
Renamed from "Very Berry Overnight Oats".

title: Buckwheat Granola Bars
description: No-bake bars of rolled oats, ground almonds, sunflower and pumpkin seeds, pistachios, cacao nibs and goji berries bound with almond butter, agave and coconut oil, studded with dried apricots and Medjool dates. Pressed, chilled and cut into fifteen.
keeps_note: Keeps a week in an airtight container in the refrigerator, or freezes.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 tablespoon melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil, plus 2 teaspoons for brushing
ingredients.prep_note: melted; includes 2 teaspoons for brushing the dish

ingredients.raw_text: 1/2 cup buckwheat groats, soaked in water for 20 minutes, drained, and rinsed
ingredients.estimate_basis: the card reads "1/2 oz cup"; taken as 1/2 cup

instructions.text: Brush a 10 x 6- to 7-inch dish with coconut oil and line it with enough parchment paper to hang over the sides. Set aside.

In a large bowl, combine the oats, ground almonds, seeds, pistachio nuts, cacao nibs, and goji berries, and stir well. Add the soaked buckwheat to the bowl and combine. Stir in the apricots and dates.
In a small bowl, combine the almond butter, agave nectar, and coconut oil. Warm gently until loose and mix with a fork.
Pour the almond butter mixture over the dry ingredients and stir well so that everything is moist.
Transfer the granola to the prepared dish and press it down firmly. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for several hours, then lift it out using the overhanging paper. Peel the paper off.
Cut the granola into 2-inch bars using a sharp knife. Store them in a covered container in the refrigerator.

notes: Chills overnight before cutting. The bars keep for a week refrigerated and freeze well, so one batch covers several breakfasts.
household_edits: Raw honey swapped for raw agave nectar so the recipe is vegan.

title: Blackberry Coconut Slice
description: A no-bake slice with a pressed crust of coconut flour, ground almonds, hazelnuts and almonds, topped with blended blackberries and strawberries set with creamed coconut and coconut oil, finished with grated cacao nibs.
keeps_note: Chills firm and cuts cleanly; keeps several days refrigerated.

ingredients.raw_text: 1/2 cup melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil, plus 1 tablespoon for brushing
ingredients.prep_note: melted; includes 1 tablespoon for brushing the pan

ingredients.raw_text: 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons raw coconut flour

ingredients.estimate_basis: one lemon yields about 3 tablespoons

ingredients.raw_text: 1/4 cup melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil

instructions.text: Brush an 8-inch baking pan with coconut oil and line it with parchment paper. Set aside.
To make the crust, combine the coconut flour, ground almonds, nuts, and sugar in a mixing bowl.
Gently warm the coconut oil with the maple syrup on the lowest setting in the microwave for 1 minute, or in a small saucepan over gentle heat. Stir the melted ingredients into the dry ones.
Press the mixture into the bottom of the prepared pan. Chill in the refrigerator for an hour, or until the mixture has hardened.
Meanwhile, make the topping. Blend the blackberries and strawberries in a blender, then blend in the coconut flour, lemon juice, and coconut milk.
Gently warm the creamed coconut with the coconut oil and maple syrup, and combine well. Add to the ingredients in the blender and blend everything for a few seconds.
When the crust has chilled, spoon the blackberry mixture evenly over the top. Cover and chill again for about 2 hours. The topping will not be particularly firm but should be firm enough to cut.
Grate cacao nibs over the top of the chilled mixture and cut it into 8 oblongs or 16 squares with a sharp knife.

notes: Chills twice — an hour for the crust and about two hours once topped. For a summer version, use a mix of raspberries and strawberries.
household_edits: Renamed from "Natural Blackberry Bars" — "natural" says nothing about the dish.

title: Kale, Apple, and Carrot Breakfast Salad
description: A crunchy raw salad of kale, red apple and carrot with Medjool dates and walnuts, dressed with apple cider vinegar, stone-ground mustard and maple syrup, and scattered with sesame, hemp and sunflower seeds. For mornings when you don't want anything sweet.
keeps_note: Kale holds up dressed; keeps a couple of days. Add the seeds just before eating.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 large red-skinned apple, such as Red Delicious, cored and chopped
3 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin canola oil

instructions.text: To make the dressing, combine the dressing ingredients in a screw-top jar or small mixing bowl. Shake or stir well.
Put the kale into a serving bowl or two individual dishes. Add the apple and carrot, and stir in the dates and walnuts.
Pour the dressing over the salad and mix together. Sprinkle with the seeds to serve.

notes: Unhulled seeds give more minerals and fiber; hulled work just as well.
household_edits: Renamed from "Wake-Up Salad" to say what is in it.

title: Beet and Pomegranate Smoothie Bowl
description: Raw beet blended with spinach, orange juice, pomegranate seeds and coconut yogurt into a deep red breakfast bowl, topped with buckwheat groats and orange slices.
keeps_note: Blended fruit separates and dulls; make it the morning you want it.

ingredients.estimate_basis: one orange yields about 1/4 cup of juice
two slices is about a quarter of an orange

instructions.text: Put the beet in a blender with the spinach, 2 tablespoons of the pomegranate seeds, and half the water. Blend until smooth.
Add the rest of the water, the orange juice, agave nectar, 1/3 cup of the yogurt, and the wheatgrass powder to the blender. Blend again.
Pour the smoothie into a serving bowl and chill for an hour or so, if you have time.
Drizzle the remaining yogurt over the smoothie. Sprinkle with the groats and decorate with the orange slices and remaining seeds.

notes: Raspberries stand in for the pomegranate seeds out of season.
household_edits: Raw honey swapped for raw agave nectar so the recipe is vegan.

title: Berry and Mango Smoothie Bowl
description: Strawberries, blackberries and raspberries blended with banana, hemp milk, coconut oil and ground almonds, then topped with kiwi, mango, walnuts, chia and sesame seeds.
keeps_note: Blended banana browns and separates within hours.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 small mango, peeled, pitted, and chopped

instructions.text: Put the strawberries, blackberries, raspberries, half the banana, the hemp milk, coconut oil, and ground almonds into a blender and blend until smooth.
Pour into a bowl and place the remaining ingredients on top to serve.

notes: The topping is a free hand — use whatever fruit and nuts are in season.
household_edits: Renamed from "Morning Power Bowl Smoothie" to name the fruit.

title: Matcha and Avocado Green Smoothie
description: Spinach, banana, avocado and kiwi blended with almond milk and matcha into a thick green smoothie bowl, topped with slivered almonds and maca powder.
keeps_note: Avocado and banana brown quickly once blended.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 small ripe avocado, peeled, pitted, and coarsely chopped
ingredients.prep_note: small, ripe, peeled, pitted, and coarsely chopped

instructions.text: Blend the spinach, banana, avocado, and one of the kiwis in a blender with half the milk until you have a puree.
Add the agave nectar, matcha, wheatgrass, and remaining milk to the blender and blend until smooth. Pour the smoothie into your serving bowl. Chill for an hour, if you have time.
Top your smoothie with the remaining kiwi and decorate with the slivered almonds and maca powder.

household_edits: Raw honey swapped for raw agave nectar so the recipe is vegan.
Renamed from "Matcha Power Smoothie".

title: Beet, Plum, and Grape Juice
description: Juiced raw beet blended with plums, red grapes and ground flaxseed — a deep red, earthy-sweet drink that takes five minutes and a juicer.
keeps_note: The recipe says serve immediately, and it means it — fresh juice separates and oxidizes fast.

instructions.text: Feed the beets through a juicer. Put the flaxseed into a blender and blend until finely ground. Add the beet juice, plums, grapes, and water, and blend until smooth. Pour into a glass, add ice if using, and serve immediately.

notes: Needs a juicer for the beets; the rest is done in a blender.
household_edits: Renamed from "Power Gulp" to say what is in the glass.

title: Raw Vegetable Spring Rolls with Coconut Dip
description: Rice paper rolls packed with raw bell pepper, cucumber, bok choy, carrot, scallion and celery, cut into halves and served with a cumin and coriander coconut yogurt dip. Nothing is cooked.
keeps_note: Rice paper goes gummy and the vegetables weep — roll them the day you eat them.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 yellow bell peppers, halved, seeded, and thinly sliced
1 1/4 red bell peppers, halved, seeded, and thinly sliced
3/4 cucumber, halved, seeded and thinly sliced
2 1/2 carrots, peeled and cut into 4-inch sticks

instructions.text: Soak a spring roll wrapper for 10 seconds, or until just pliable, then smooth it onto a cutting board. Arrange a tenth of all the vegetables on the lower center of the wrap. Sprinkle with a little of the coconut aminos sauce.
Tuck each side of the wrapper into the center, then fold the lower edge up to enclose the vegetables, keeping them in a tight bunch as you roll up to the top. Repeat with the remaining wrappers.
Using a sharp knife, cut each roll in half until you have 20 halves, and arrange them on a serving dish.

To make the dip, combine the yogurt in a mixing bowl with the coconut aminos sauce, cumin, coriander, garlic, salt, and half the cilantro leaves. Spoon the dip into a serving dish and serve alongside the spring rolls, garnished with the remaining cilantro.

notes: For another occasion, serve the rolls with a nutty dip — swirl raw cashew butter into nut milk with a dash of coconut aminos.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings (16 half-rolls) to 5 servings (20 half-rolls), the VegBatch standard.
Renamed from "Spring Rolls in the Raw".

title: Chilled Beet and Watermelon Soup
description: A raw blended soup of beet, carrot and watermelon sharpened with lemon, thickened with grated beet and carrot, and finished with coconut yogurt and fresh dill. Served cold as a summer gazpacho.
keeps_note: A chilled blended soup — keeps 2 to 3 days covered and is better cold.

ingredients.estimate_basis: a lemon yields about 3 tablespoons

instructions.text: Blend two-thirds of the beet, carrot, and watermelon in a blender with the lemon juice and most of the water until smooth. Add the salt and pepper, then add the water a little at a time, and blend again until you have a medium-thick soup texture. Pour the soup into a large bowl.
Grate the remaining beet and carrot, and stir into the soup. Stir half of the remaining watermelon into the soup with half the dill.

Pour the soup into five serving bowls and drizzle with the yogurt. Sprinkle the remaining watermelon pieces over the top and sprinkle with the rest of the dill. Chill in the refrigerator before serving.

notes: Served chilled as a summer gazpacho, or warmed gently in colder months.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.

title: Garlic and Herb Coconut Yogurt Dip
description: Homemade coconut yogurt drained overnight to a thick Greek-style consistency, then stirred through with garlic and soft herbs and served with raw vegetable sticks and chopped pistachios.
keeps_note: The drained yogurt keeps several days; cut the vegetable sticks fresh.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/2 cups frozen raw white coconut meat (about 10 1/2 ounces), thawed if frozen
ingredients.prep_note: thawed if frozen; or the white meat of 1/2 fresh coconut

ingredients.raw_text: 2 tablespoons mixed fresh soft herbs, such as parsley, cilantro, tarragon, or chives
14 ounces mixed vegetable sticks, such as asparagus, red bell pepper, cucumber, baby zucchini, babycorn, carrots, and broccoli florets
ingredients.prep_note: asparagus, red bell pepper, cucumber, baby zucchini, babycorn, carrots, broccoli florets

instructions.text: Process the coconut meat with half the coconut water in a food processor until it is thoroughly blended, then add the rest of the water and blend again until smooth.
Break open the probiotic capsule and sprinkle the contents into the food processor; pulse for a few seconds.
Pour the mixture into a large, wide-neck jar. Put the lid on and let stand in a warm kitchen overnight, until you have a yogurt mixture.

Spoon the yogurt into a strainer lined with cheesecloth and set over a bowl. Refrigerate for 24 hours, or until the yogurt remaining in the strainer is a consistency similar to a soft cheese. Discard any liquid in the bowl.
Stir the garlic and herbs into the yogurt and season with salt and pepper, if using.
Divide among four bowls, drizzle with the oil, and sprinkle with the chopped nuts. Serve with vegetable sticks for dipping.

notes: Ferments overnight and then drains for 24 hours, so start it two days before you want it.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 4 servings — a dip, not a meal.
