title: Raw Sauerkraut
description: Red and green cabbage kneaded with carrot, fresh ginger and sea salt, packed into a jar and left to ferment at room temperature for a week. Ten minutes of work and then patience.
keeps_note: Keeps for several weeks in a cool place once fermented — it is a preserve.

ingredients.raw_text: 2 small carrots, peeled and thinly sliced
1 1/2-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and finely chopped

instructions.text: Mix all the ingredients together in a large plastic mixing bowl.
Firmly knead the mixture for 5 minutes, until the vegetables begin to release their juice and become softer.
Pack the mixture into a 24-ounce jar with a lid. Press the top of the mixture down and fill up with enough water to completely cover the vegetables.

Secure the lid on the jar and keep it at room temperature for a week. Every day, open the jar and press the sauerkraut down again — you should see air bubbles coming out of the top of the mixture. Make sure all the vegetables are completely covered in the liquid.
After a week, you can eat the sauerkraut, or store it in a cool place for several weeks.

notes: Ferments for a week before it is ready. Beets work in place of the carrot, and caraway seeds or cumin give it more of a kick.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 8 servings — a preserve, not a meal.

title: Cucumber Sushi Rolls with Spicy Cashew Dip
description: Two kinds of raw sushi — hollowed cucumber barrels filled with cauliflower rice and avocado, and thin cucumber strips rolled around spinach, zucchini, carrot and cashew cream — with a wasabi cashew dip and a blended mushroom dressing.
keeps_note: Cucumber weeps once cut and rolled; assemble and eat the same day.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 teaspoons cold-pressed extra virgin sesame oil
3/4 small red bell pepper, finely chopped
3/4 cup raw cashew nuts, soaked in water for 1 hour, drained, and rinsed

instructions.text: Cut off the ends of the cucumber so that you have a center section that is one width. Cut into ten pieces, 1 1/2 inches long. Scoop out the seed section and about half the flesh from each piece to form hollow sushi rolls. Set aside.
Put the cauliflower, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and salt into a food processor and pulse until the mixture resembles cooked rice.
Mash the avocado in a small bowl, adding salt, if using.

Arrange your cucumber shapes on a board or serving plate and fill each one with some cauliflower rice, pressing it toward the sides. Add some avocado and press it into the rice. Sprinkle with some scallions and red bell pepper.

To make the dip, put the soaked nuts into a food processor and process for several minutes, until you have a creamy consistency. Beat in the ginger and wasabi paste, and transfer to a small serving dish.

Start making the cucumber wrappers. Trim off the ends of the cucumber as before. Cut the cucumber in half, then cut each half into thin strips lengthwise and discard the first skin layer. You will need 30 strips for the ten rolls.

To make each roll, arrange three cucumber strips on a board. Place a tenth of the spinach leaves at one end in a line from left to right. Arrange a tenth of the zucchini and carrot slices on top, again in a line from left to right, and a tenth of the cashew cream.
Starting with the filled end, roll up the cucumber strip until you have a filled tube. Transfer the roll to a serving board or plate and continue to make the rest of the sushi.

To make the dressing, blend the mushrooms, salt, and water in a clean processor until you have a smooth sauce. Add a little more water to make a soy sauce consistency and stir in the ginger. Serve in a small bowl alongside the sushi.

notes: Two separate techniques on one plate — hollowed cucumber barrels and rolled cucumber strips. Neither needs a sushi mat.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings (16 rolls) to 5 servings (20 rolls), the VegBatch standard.
Renamed from "Cool Cucumber Sushi".

title: Chopped Vegetable Salad with Cashew Ranch
description: Finely chopped tomato, cucumber, red onion, carrot, yellow pepper and radish tossed with soft herbs, lemon and olive oil, under a thick ranch dressing built from soaked cashews and coconut milk instead of buttermilk.
keeps_note: Dressing keeps a week; the chopped salad holds 2 days if you dress it as you serve.

ingredients.raw_text: 3/4 cup mixed chopped soft herbs, such as parsley, mint, and cilantro
1/3 cup cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil
1 cup raw cashew nuts, soaked in water for 2 hours, drained, and rinsed

instructions.text: To make the dressing, put the soaked nuts, vinegar, 1/4 cup of the coconut milk, the garlic, and salt into a blender. Blend until you have a smooth paste. Add more coconut milk, a little at a time, until you have a fairly thick mix — it should be a cross between a dip and a pouring consistency. Stir in the scallions and parsley.
To make the salad, finely chop the vegetables and put them into a large serving bowl or smaller individual ones. Stir in all the remaining salad ingredients and serve.

notes: Vary the vegetables with the season — corn kernels work in place of the yellow bell pepper.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.
Renamed from "Jewel Salad with Ranch Dressing" to say what it is.

title: Cucumber and Buckwheat Yogurt Jars
description: Layered jars of coconut yogurt with mint, raisins, walnuts, soaked buckwheat groats and squeezed cucumber. A savoury yogurt pot built to travel.
keeps_note: Built in sealed jars and chilled — holds 2 to 3 days if the cucumber is squeezed dry.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 cup raw buckwheat groats, soaked in water for 20 minutes, drained, and rinsed

instructions.text: Wrap the cucumber pieces in paper towels and squeeze to release the moisture — the paper towels should end up soaked.
Mix the yogurt, mint, salt, and pepper together in a bowl.

Divide the ingredients evenly among five 9- to 10-ounce jars with lids. Layer with the raisins, half the walnuts, the soaked groats, three-quarters of the cucumber, and the yogurt mixture. Garnish with the remaining cucumber and walnuts.
Divide the mint leaves among each of the jars and chill for 30 minutes before serving.

notes: Squeezing the cucumber dry is what keeps the jars from going watery. Finely chopped scallions and a little crushed garlic work in place of the mint.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.

title: Eggplant, Lettuce, and Avocado Sandwich
description: Marinated eggplant slices dehydrated until crisp and stacked with cashew cheese, red pepper pesto, smashed avocado, lettuce and tomato — a sandwich with no bread in it.
keeps_note: Assembled it goes soft fast — but the eggplant, cheese and pesto all keep, so build them to order.

ingredients.raw_text: 5 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil
5 teaspoons minced fresh mild red chile
1 1/4 cups raw cashew nuts, soaked in water for 1 hour, drained, and rinsed
2 1/2 small red bell peppers, coarsely chopped
5 pieces sun-dried tomatoes, soaked in water for 10 minutes, drained, and rinsed

ingredients.estimate_basis: half a lime yields about 1 tablespoon

ingredients.raw_text: 10 Boston or small butter lettuce leaves

instructions.text: You will need a dehydrator for this recipe. If you don't have one, an electric oven may have a setting low enough — the defrost setting or slightly higher, or a designated dehydrate setting. Check the temperature with an oven thermometer before dehydrating in a standard oven.

Slice each eggplant into eight long slices about 1/4 inch thick, and discard the two skin sides. Combine the rest of the crispy eggplant ingredients in a small bowl and brush each eggplant slice with the mixture.

Put the eggplant in a nonmetallic dish and cover. Let marinate for 2 hours, then drain and layer on a dehydrator tray. (If using the oven, use a nonstick oven pan.) Dehydrate on low (115°F) for 8 hours, turning the slices halfway.

Meanwhile, make the cashew cheese. Blend the soaked nuts in a food processor with the remaining cashew cheese ingredients until you have a smooth paste. Thin with a little water if necessary, and blend again. Remove the cheese from the processor and set aside in a bowl.
Make the red pepper pesto. Add the red bell pepper, soaked tomatoes, pine nuts, and salt and pepper to a processor and pulse until you have a thick paste with small visible pieces in it.
Before you assemble your sandwiches, make the smashed avocado. In a small bowl, mash the avocado flesh with the rest of the ingredients until you have a textured puree.

Prepare your sandwiches on your serving plates. For each sandwich, start with two slices of eggplant side by side. Top with a fifth of the cashew cheese and two lettuce leaves. Smooth on a fifth of the red pepper pesto and arrange a fifth of the tomato slices on top. Add a fifth of the avocado mixture and smooth down, then finish with two more eggplant slices. Serve immediately.

notes: Needs a dehydrator, 2 hours of marinating and 8 hours of drying, so start the day before. The eggplant, cashew cheese and pesto all keep — build the sandwiches only when you are ready to eat.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 2 sandwiches to 5, the VegBatch standard.

title: Vegetable Fries with Cashew Dip
description: Butternut squash and zucchini cut into sticks and dehydrated until crisp, served with a cashew, tahini and carrot dip thinned with almond milk.
keeps_note: Dehydrated sticks store crisp in an airtight container; the dip keeps several days.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 tablespoon cold-pressed extra virgin canola oil
1/2 cup raw cashew nuts, soaked in water for 2 hours, drained, and rinsed

instructions.text: You will need a dehydrator for this recipe. If you don't have one, an electric oven may have a setting low enough — the defrost setting or slightly higher, or a designated dehydrate setting. Check the temperature with an oven thermometer before dehydrating in a standard oven.
Cut the squash in half between the thin neck and the bulbous bottom. Reserve the bulbous bottom for another dish. Peel the squash and cut it into thin sticks.

Toss the zucchini and squash sticks with the canola oil, salt, and pepper, and arrange them on a dehydrator tray. (If using the oven, use a nonstick oven pan.) Dehydrate on high (140°F) for an hour, then low (115°F) for 8 hours, turning the sticks halfway.
Meanwhile, make the cashew dip. Add the soaked nuts to a blender with the tahini and lemon juice, then process until you have a coarse butter.

Add the garlic, carrot, salt, and pepper to the blender and process again until you have a pâté consistency. Remove the mixture and stir in the nut milk a little at a time, until you have a dip-like consistency — you may not need all the milk, or you may need a little more.
When the sticks are crispy and like French fries, remove them from the dehydrator and serve with the dip.

notes: Nine hours in the dehydrator, so plan it the day before. Sweet potato works in place of the squash or zucchini.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 2 servings — fries and a dip, not a meal.

title: Raw Miso Soup with Radish and Sprouts
original_title: Miso Soup with Radish and Seed Sprouts
description: Unpasteurized miso blended cold with garlic, ginger and rice vinegar, poured over thinly sliced scallion, snow peas, radish and baby corn, and topped with coconut shards, pea shoots and home-sprouted sunflower seeds.
keeps_note: The miso broth keeps 3 days; slice and add the vegetables as you serve.

ingredients.raw_text: 2 1/2 tablespoons unshelled sunflower seeds suitable for sprouting

ingredients.prep_note: added gradually to reach 6 1/4 cups of soup

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin sesame oil, to serve

instructions.text: Start sprouting the sunflower seeds three days before you want to make the soup. Put them into a shallow dish lined with plenty of thick paper towels. Sprinkle lukewarm water over the seeds and cover with more paper. Sprinkle again. Let stand in a dark, warm place. Check each day that the seeds are still slightly damp. When they begin to sprout, remove the top layer of paper and bring into the light. The sprouts can be eaten when they are about 3/8 inch long.
To make the soup, blend the miso paste with the garlic, ginger, rice vinegar, and water in a blender. Add more water until you have about 6 1/4 cups and stir well. Pour the soup into five bowls.
Thinly slice the scallions, snow peas, radishes, and corn, and arrange the vegetables over the soup. Top with the coconut shards, pea shoots, and seed sprouts. Drizzle with the sesame oil to serve.

notes: The sunflower seeds need three days to sprout, so start well ahead. Buy unpasteurized miso — many supermarket brands are heated above raw temperature. Sprouted seeds are not recommended for young children, older adults, pregnant women, or anyone with a weakened immune system.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.
Renamed from "Miso Soup with Radish and Seed Sprouts" to flag that it is raw.

title: Vegetable and Seed Crackers
description: Crackers made from the pulp left over after juicing carrots, celery and radishes, bound with flaxseed, sunflower and pumpkin seeds and soaked chia, then dehydrated until crisp.
keeps_note: Dehydrated and stored airtight — these are built to keep.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 tablespoon chia seeds, soaked in 3 tablespoons water for 1 hour
ingredients.prep_note: soaked in 3 tablespoons water for 1 hour

instructions.text: You will need a dehydrator for this recipe. If you don't have one, an electric oven may have a setting low enough — the defrost setting or slightly higher, or a designated dehydrate setting. Check the temperature with an oven thermometer before dehydrating in a standard oven.
Juice the carrots, celery stalks, and radishes, and save the juice to drink. Remove the pulp from the juicer and put it into a mixing bowl. You should have about 1 1/2 mugfuls of pulp.
Stir the rest of the ingredients into the mixing bowl, including the soaked seeds and their water. Combine thoroughly, adding a little water if the mix seems dry or doesn't stick together well.

Spread the mixture thinly and evenly on a dehydrator tray lined with a nonstick sheet. (If using the oven, use a nonstick oven pan.) Dehydrate on low (115°F) for 4 hours. Turn the mixture over, score it into 16 crackers, and dehydrate on low for an additional 4 hours, or until the crackers are crisped to your preference.
Let the crackers cool, then break along the knife scores. Store the crackers in an airtight container.

notes: This is a use for juicing pulp rather than a recipe you shop for. With no juicer, pulse the vegetables in a processor and squeeze the juice out by hand, or press the mixture in a strainer.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 16 crackers — a batch, not a meal.

title: Seaweed and Sesame Salad
description: Mixed dried seaweed reconstituted and dressed with sesame oil, rice vinegar, coconut aminos, chile, mirin and miso, finished with scallion, radish and sesame seeds.
keeps_note: Dressed seaweed holds its texture — keeps 2 days chilled.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 (3/4-ounce) package of mixed dried seaweed, soaked in water for 5-10 minutes
ingredients.prep_note: soaked in water for 5 to 10 minutes

ingredients.raw_text: 1 tablespoon cold-pressed extra virgin sesame oil
2 teaspoons mirin (Japanese rice wine) or sherry

instructions.text: While the seaweed mixture is soaking, make the dressing. Add the sesame oil, rice vinegar, coconut aminos sauce, chile, mirin, and miso paste to a screw-top jar or small bowl and shake or stir vigorously to combine.
Once the seaweed is tender and reconstituted, drain it thoroughly in a colander and rinse.
Divide the seaweed between two shallow bowls and drizzle the dressing over it, tossing lightly.
Sprinkle the chopped scallion and radish over the salad and garnish with the sesame seeds to serve.

notes: Dried seaweed mixes are sold in Asian groceries and health food stores — wakame, dulse, agar agar, miyoek, chondrus and kelp all work.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 2 servings — a small side salad, not a meal.

title: Oat Bread with Chia Seeds
description: A dehydrated loaf of rolled oats, oat and buckwheat flour, ground walnuts and pumpkin seeds, bound with psyllium and soaked chia, and flavoured with green olives and dried herbs. Sliced before drying so it breaks cleanly.
keeps_note: Dehydrated and stored airtight — a whole loaf's worth of slices keeps well.

ingredients.raw_text: 2 teaspoons sun-dried herbes de Provence (or half-dried parsley and half-dried rosemary)
ingredients.prep_note: sun-dried; or half dried parsley and half dried rosemary

ingredients.raw_text: 1 tablespoon cold-pressed extra virgin canola oil
2 tablespoons chia seeds, soaked in 1/2 cup water for 20 minutes
ingredients.prep_note: soaked in 1/2 cup water for 20 minutes

instructions.text: You will need a dehydrator for this recipe. If you don't have one, an electric oven may have a setting low enough — the defrost setting or slightly higher, or a designated dehydrate setting. Check the temperature with an oven thermometer before dehydrating in a standard oven.
Combine the oats, oat flour, buckwheat flour, pumpkin seeds, ground walnuts, and psyllium in a large mixing bowl. Stir in the olives, herbs, salt, pepper, and canola oil. Mix thoroughly.

Add the soaked chia seeds and their water to the mixing bowl and knead the mix. If the dough doesn't come together, add a tablespoon of water and knead again. Repeat if necessary. To make a fairly dry dough, 1/4 cup of water should be enough.

On a board, form the dough into an oblong shape and transfer to a nonstick dehydrator sheet. (If using the oven, use a nonstick oven pan.) Using a sharp knife, score slices along the bread, cutting two-thirds of the way into the loaf.

Place the sheet on a dehydrator tray and dehydrate on high for an hour (140°F), then turn to low (115°F) and continue dehydrating for 6 hours. Cut slices along the scores you made and dehydrate for an additional hour on low, or until you have firm slices.
Store the oat bread in an airtight container.

notes: About eight hours in the dehydrator. Ground Brazil nuts or hazelnuts work in place of the walnuts.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 1 loaf — a bake, not a meal.

title: Seed and Vegetable Flatbreads
description: Ground sunflower seeds, walnuts and oats blended with zucchini, carrot, celery, baby corn and red pepper, pressed thin and dehydrated into pliable flatbreads rather than crackers.
keeps_note: Cooled and stored airtight — these are made to keep.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 small carrot, peeled and coarsely chopped
1 tablespoon cold-pressed extra virgin canola oil

instructions.text: You will need a dehydrator for this recipe. If you don't have one, an electric oven may have a setting low enough — the defrost setting or slightly higher, or a designated dehydrate setting. Check the temperature with an oven thermometer before dehydrating in a standard oven.
Put the flaxseed and hemp seeds in a mixing bowl with 3 tablespoons of the sunflower seeds.

Grind the rest of the sunflower seeds, the walnuts, and oats in a food processor and transfer to the mixing bowl. Add the zucchini, carrot, celery, and corn to the processor and pulse until they are finely chopped. Add the red bell pepper and pulse for 1 to 2 seconds.
Transfer the vegetable mixture to the bowl and stir in the canola oil and salt. Add 1 to 2 tablespoons of water if the mixture seems dry. Stir again.

Transfer the mixture to two nonstick dehydrator sheets on dehydrator trays and press down to about 1/4 to 3/8 inch thick. Dehydrate on high (140°F) for an hour, then turn to low (115°F) and dehydrate for an additional 2 to 3 hours, or until the flatbread feels fairly dry to the touch.

Flip the flatbread over with a large flat spatula and score with a sharp knife to make eight large squares. Dehydrate on low for an additional 2 to 3 hours, or until the mixture is dry but still has some give — you want flatbread, not crackers.
Break or cut the flatbreads along the scores you made. Let them cool completely, then store in an airtight container.

notes: Stop while they still give — dried too far they become crackers. Good with sliced tomato and avocado, or cashew butter and cucumber.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 8 flatbreads — a batch, not a meal.
Renamed from "Seedburst Flatbreads".

title: Cucumber Noodle Bowl with Thai Dressing
original_title: Cucumber Noodle Bowl with Thai Dressing
description: Spiralized beet and cucumber with kale, red onion and carrot under a sesame, miso, lime and peanut butter dressing, topped with peanuts rolled in ground seaweed and fresh coconut flakes.
keeps_note: Spiralized cucumber waters out within hours — dress and eat it the same day.

ingredients.raw_text: 2 1/2 small carrots, peeled and thinly sliced
5/8 cup fresh coconut flakes, to garnish
2 1/2 tablespoons fresh cilantro leaves, to garnish
5 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin sesame oil

ingredients.estimate_basis: half a lime yields about 1 tablespoon

instructions.text: Arrange all but a few strands of the beet in five serving bowls. Add all of the cucumber strands.
Add the kale to the bowls and top with the onion and carrot.
To make the dressing, combine all the ingredients in a small bowl and mix well. Spoon it over the beet salad.
Run the peanuts under cold water, then pat them dry so they are just slightly damp. On a plate, roll them in the seaweed until they are thoroughly coated, then sprinkle them over the salad.
Add the coconut flakes and cilantro leaves to the salad. Garnish with the remaining beet strands to serve.

notes: Raw cashew butter and cashews work in place of the peanut butter and peanuts.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 2 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.

title: Cauliflower Salad with Apple and Nuts
original_title: Cauliflower Salad with Apple and Nuts
description: Raw cauliflower florets with chopped red apple, sunflower and sesame seeds and walnuts, over spiralized sweet potato and red onion, under a horseradish and dill coconut yogurt dressing.
keeps_note: Cauliflower and sweet potato hold their crunch — keeps 2 to 3 days if dressed as you serve.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 large red-skinned dessert apples, such as Red Delicious, cored and chopped
1 1/4 large sweet potatoes, peeled and spiralized
1 1/4 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin canola oil
2 1/2 teaspoons chopped fresh dill, to garnish

ingredients.estimate_basis: a lemon yields about 3 tablespoons

instructions.text: Put the cauliflower florets into a large bowl. Add three-quarters of the apple, all of the seeds, and 2 tablespoons of the walnuts.
Beat all the dressing ingredients together in a small bowl and pour it over the cauliflower mixture. Stir well until everything is coated.
Divide the sweet potato spirals among five serving dishes and sprinkle the onion spirals on top. Drizzle with the canola oil, then add the salt and pepper.
Spoon the cauliflower mixture into the serving dishes. Top with the remaining apple and walnuts, and garnish with the dill to serve.

notes: The sweet potato is eaten raw, spiralized — no cooking anywhere in this.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.

title: Raw Vegetable Lasagne
description: Thin zucchini slices marinated in oil and balsamic, layered on the plate with macadamia nut cheese, a tomato paste sauce, avocado and pine nut pesto, spinach and sliced tomato. Built cold, no pasta and no oven.
keeps_note: Layered straight onto plates and served — it does not travel or hold.

ingredients.estimate_basis: half a lime yields about 1 tablespoon

ingredients.raw_text: 5 teaspoons pine nuts, toasted, to garnish

instructions.text: To make the zucchini layer, place the zucchini in a dish that will hold the slices in one layer. Cover the slices with the oil, vinegar, and salt, making sure that each slice is well covered, then set aside for up to 1 hour to soften and absorb the flavors.
To make the cheese layer, pulse all the ingredients in a blender until you have a smooth, light paste.

To make the tomato sauce, combine all the ingredients in a small bowl, then add about 2 tablespoons of cold water and mix thoroughly. Add a little more water until you have a pouring consistency. Add salt, if using.

To make the avocado pesto layer, put the pine nuts into an electric mini chopper or blender and process for a few seconds, or until chopped but not pureed. Add the avocado chunks, basil leaves, garlic, lime juice, and salt and pulse until you have a lightly textured mixture. Slice the tomatoes so that you have six inside slices from each. Discard the outer slices.

Layer the five lasagne servings directly onto plates. Arrange a tenth of the zucchini slices in a rectangle on the center of each plate. For each plate, top with a tenth of the spinach leaves, then spoon a tenth of the nut cheese over them. Add a tenth of the tomato slices and top them with a tenth of the avocado pesto. For each plate, add another tenth of the tomato slices, a tenth of the cheese, a tenth of the spinach, and a tenth of the avocado pesto. Finish by placing the remaining zucchini slices on top of each lasagne.
Drizzle the sauce over the five lasagne and garnish with toasted pine nuts and basil leaves.

notes: The zucchini needs an hour in the marinade, which is most of the stated time. Everything else is assembly.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 2 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.

title: Avocado, Asparagus, and Sprout Salad
description: Home-sprouted green peas and quinoa with baby spinach, raw asparagus tips, plum tomatoes and watercress, layered with sliced avocado and a coarse avocado and pine nut puree, under a mustard vinaigrette.
keeps_note: Avocado browns and the leaves wilt once dressed — assemble to order.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 cups dry green peas suitable for sprouting
1 1/4 cups whole quinoa seeds suitable for sprouting
5 ripe avocados, pitted, peeled, and sliced into bite-size pieces
ingredients.prep_note: ripe, pitted, peeled, and sliced into bite-size pieces

ingredients.raw_text: 3 3/4 teaspoons cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil
5 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: To sprout the peas, put them into a wide-neck glass jar and soak overnight in lukewarm water, covered with cheesecloth or a similar material. In the morning, drain and rinse the peas and fill the jar with fresh water. Drain and rinse the peas twice a day for five days, until they sprout. Rinse and drain to use.
To sprout the quinoa, use the same method as the peas but soak them for only 4 hours. They will sprout in about two days.
Arrange the spinach, all but ten of the asparagus tips, and the plum tomatoes in five serving dishes with most of the watercress.
Arrange three-quarters of the avocado slices in the dishes with the remaining watercress and the pea and quinoa sprouts. Sprinkle three-quarters of the pine nuts on top.
In a small bowl, mash the remaining avocado with the remaining pine nuts, fifteen of the basil sprigs, and the olive oil until you have a coarse puree.
Make the dressing by thoroughly combining the ingredients in a small dish. Spoon most of it over the salad.
Finish the salad by arranging two asparagus tips in the center of each dish, followed by a fifth of the avocado puree and a basil sprig. Drizzle with the rest of the dressing to serve.

notes: The peas need five days to sprout and the quinoa two, so start well ahead. Slivered almonds or chopped hazelnuts work in place of the pine nuts. Sprouted seeds are not recommended for young children, older adults, pregnant women, or anyone with a weakened immune system.
household_edits: Raw honey swapped for raw agave nectar so the recipe is vegan.
Scaled from the book's 2 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.
Renamed from "Avocado Hero Salad".

title: Fruit and Vegetable Kabobs
description: Raw fennel, turnip, butternut squash, yellow pepper, papaya, mango and fresh coconut marinated in orange juice, agave and coconut aminos, threaded onto skewers and served over herb salad greens with a coconut yogurt dressing.
keeps_note: The marinated fruit and vegetables hold 2 days; thread and dress as you serve.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 small Florence fennel bulbs, divided into leaves
1 1/4 small turnips, peeled and thinly sliced
1/8 butternut squash, peeled and thinly sliced
ingredients.estimate_basis: the book's 1/16 scaled up, rounded to an eighth

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 yellow bell peppers, seeded and cut into squares
1 1/4 papayas, peeled, seeded, and cut into cubes
ingredients.prep_note: peeled, seeded, and cut into cubes

ingredients.raw_text: 5/8 mango, peeled and cut into chunks
2 1/2 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil
3 1/8 cups fresh herb and salad greens, such as sorrel, mizuna, flat-leaf parsley, cilantro, and celery
ingredients.prep_note: sorrel, mizuna, flat-leaf parsley, cilantro, and celery

instructions.text: You will need five wooden skewers for this recipe.
To make the kabobs, put all the fruit and vegetables into a nonmetallic dish and mix well.
In a small bowl, combine the marinade ingredients, then pour them over the kabob mixture. Stir well, cover, and set aside for 3 to 5 hours.
Shake any excess marinade off the fruit and vegetables, and thread them onto five wooden skewers.

Arrange the salad greens on five serving plates and sprinkle with the poppy seeds. Combine the yogurt, coconut milk, vinegar, garlic, and salt in a separate small bowl and drizzle the dressing over the salad.
Serve the kabobs alongside the salad.

notes: Three to five hours in the marinade. Salsify or daikon work in place of the turnip.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.

title: Kelp, Orange, and Mango Bowl
description: Rehydrated kelp tossed with cucumber, orange sections, chile, carrot, mango and bok choy in a lime and miso dressing, finished with chopped peanuts, mint and cilantro.
keeps_note: Kelp and carrot hold their bite — keeps 2 days chilled.

ingredients.raw_text: 5/16 ounce dried kelp or dried kombu
1 1/4 red chiles, seeded and finely diced
1 1/4 large mangoes, peeled, pitted, and chopped

ingredients.estimate_basis: the method calls for mint that the ingredient list omits

ingredients.raw_text: grated zest and juice of 1 1/4 limes

instructions.text: Put the kelp into a bowl of water and let stand for 10 minutes to rehydrate.
Meanwhile, to make the dressing, whisk together the oil, lime zest and juice, agave nectar, and miso paste.
Halve the cucumber lengthwise and, using a teaspoon, scoop out and discard the seeds.
Peel the oranges and cut them into sections.
Coarsely chop the kelp and put into a large bowl with the cucumber, orange sections, chile, carrot, mango, bok choy, and half the mint and cilantro.
Pour in the dressing and toss well. Divide among five bowls.
Sprinkle each bowl with chopped peanuts and the remaining mint and cilantro.

notes: Nori sheets work if you can't find kelp or kombu — serve them dry, broken into shards, for extra crunch.
household_edits: Honey swapped for raw agave nectar so the recipe is vegan.
Scaled from the book's 4 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.
Renamed from "Seaweed Power Bowl".
Mint added to the ingredient list — the method uses it but the card never listed it.

title: Sweet-and-Sour Kelp Noodle Bowl
description: Raw kelp noodles over parsnip and sweet potato "rice" with soaked shiitake, bok choy and enoki mushrooms, dotted with a chile, ginger and tahini sauce and topped with sprouted adzuki and mung beans.
keeps_note: The vegetable rice and sauce both keep 2 to 3 days; assemble the bowls fresh.

ingredients.raw_text: 5/8 cup adzuki beans suitable for sprouting
5/8 cup mung beans suitable for sprouting
2 1/2 small sweet potatoes, peeled and coarsely chopped
3 3/4 tablespoons dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked in water for 15 minutes, drained, and rinsed
ingredients.prep_note: dried, soaked 15 minutes, drained, and rinsed

ingredients.raw_text: 2 1/2 mild red chiles, seeded and finely sliced
2 1/2 small medium-hot red chiles, seeded and chopped
2 1/2 teaspoons peeled and chopped fresh ginger
2 1/2 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin sesame oil

ingredients.estimate_basis: half a lime yields about 1 tablespoon

instructions.text: Start sprouting the adzuki and mung beans three days before you want to make the dish. Put the beans into a wide-neck glass jar and soak them overnight in lukewarm water, covered with cheesecloth or a similar material. In the morning, drain and rinse the beans and fill the jar with fresh water. Drain and rinse them twice a day for three days, until they sprout. Rinse and drain to use.
To make the sauce, process all the ingredients until you have a paste. Add a little water until you have a thick pouring consistency and stir well.
Put the parsnip into a food processor and process until you have rice-size pieces. Transfer to a mixing bowl. Do the same with the sweet potato and then lightly mix the two vegetables.
Chop the soaked shiitake mushrooms into small pieces and mix them into the vegetable rice.
Rinse the kelp noodles and shake to dry in a strainer. Arrange most of them in five serving bowls and top with the vegetable rice mixture.
Arrange the bok choy and enoki mushrooms on top of the rice, then dot spoonfuls of the sauce around the dish.
Finish with the chile slices, pine nuts, and bean sprouts. Finally, arrange the few remaining kelp noodles on top and serve.

notes: The beans need three days to sprout. Cauliflower works in place of the parsnip for the rice, and lentil or chickpea sprouts in place of the adzuki and mung. Sprouted beans are not recommended for young children, older adults, pregnant women, or anyone with a weakened immune system.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 2 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.
Renamed from "Sweet-and-Sour \"Stir-Fry\"" — nothing is fried, and the scare quotes were doing the work the title should.

title: Sprouted Shoots and Seeds Salad
original_title: Raw Shoots and Seeds Super Salad
description: Mixed seed and bean sprouts with pumpkin, sunflower and sesame seeds, chopped apple, dried apricots and walnuts, dressed simply with lemon zest and juice and a cold-pressed oil.
keeps_note: The book says sprouts are always best eaten fresh, and the method says serve immediately.

ingredients.raw_text: 2 to 2 1/2 cups mixed seed and bean sprouts, such as alfalfa, mung beans, soybeans, adzuki beans, chickpeas, and radish seeds
grated zest and juice of 1 lemon

instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the sprouts and seeds. Core and chop the apple and chop the apricots into small pieces. Stir the fruit into the bowl, then stir in the lemon zest and walnuts.
Make a dressing by mixing the lemon juice with the oil in a small bowl, using a fork to thoroughly combine.
Stir the dressing into the salad and serve immediately.

notes: Lentils, peas, adzuki beans, mung beans and chickpeas all sprout in four to eight days. Only eat them once sprouted. Sprouted beans are not recommended for young children, older adults, pregnant women, or anyone with a weakened immune system.
household_edits: Scaled down from the book's 6 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard. The apple and lemon were left whole rather than cut to fractions.
Renamed from "Raw Shoots and Seeds Super Salad".

title: Raw Pizza
description: A dehydrated crust of ground walnuts, seeds and buckwheat flour with celery and onion, spread with a pounded spinach, basil and pine nut sauce and topped with marinated cremini mushrooms, red onion and tomatoes.
keeps_note: The crusts keep crisp in an airtight container — top them as you eat.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 tablespoons water, plus extra if necessary
2 1/2 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil
2 1/2 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: You will need a dehydrator for this recipe. If you don't have one, an electric oven may have a setting low enough — the defrost setting or slightly higher, or a designated dehydrate setting. Check the temperature with an oven thermometer before dehydrating in a standard oven.

To make the pizza crust, pulse the walnuts, sunflower seeds, and pumpkin seeds in a food processor for a few seconds, until coarsely ground. Transfer to a mixing bowl with the hemp seeds, flaxseed, buckwheat flour, salt, and pepper, and stir.

Add the celery and onion to the processor and pulse to a puree, then spoon into the mixing bowl. Add the water and mix everything together, adding a little more water and mixing again until you have a fairly dry dough.

Shape the dough into two 9-inch circles on nonstick dehydrator sheets. (If using the oven, use a nonstick oven pan.) Dehydrate for 3 hours on low (115°F), then turn the crusts over and dehydrate for an additional 3 hours on low, or until lightly crisped and firm.

Meanwhile, start preparing the toppings. Put the mushrooms and onion into a shallow nonmetallic dish. Mix the marinade ingredients together and pour into the dish, making sure all the vegetables are coated. Cover and let stand for 2 hours to soften and absorb the flavors.
To make the spinach sauce, put all the ingredients into a mortar and pound with a pestle. For a smoother spread, you can process the ingredients in a food processor.
Spread half the sauce over each pizza crust and divide the topping ingredients between each one. Drizzle a little marinade over the pizzas and grind black pepper over the top to serve.

notes: Six hours in the dehydrator for the crusts and two hours for the marinade, so start the day before.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings (two 8-inch pizzas) to 5 servings, the VegBatch standard — the crusts are shaped a little larger rather than cut into an awkward half pizza.

title: Raw Falafel with Raw Hummus
description: Sprouted chickpeas and raw sweet potato processed with tahini, cumin, chile and ginger, rolled in sesame seeds and dehydrated into falafel balls, served with a zucchini-based raw hummus and a chopped salad.
keeps_note: Dehydrated falafel keep several days and the hummus a few — dress the salad as you serve.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 sweet potatoes, peeled and coarsely chopped
2 1/2 teaspoons peeled and chopped fresh ginger

ingredients.estimate_basis: a lemon yields about 3 tablespoons

ingredients.raw_text: 5/8 red bell pepper, seeded and sliced
15 Boston or small butter lettuce leaves
5 teaspoons cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil

instructions.text: You will need a dehydrator for this recipe. If you don't have one, an electric oven may have a setting low enough — the defrost setting or slightly higher, or a designated dehydrate setting. Check the temperature with an oven thermometer before dehydrating in a standard oven.

Start sprouting the chickpeas three to five days before making the recipe. Put the chickpeas into a jar and cover with lukewarm water. Keep in a warm, dark room. Soak for 24 hours, then drain and rinse, and drain again. Rinse and drain twice a day for three to five days. When the sprouts are about 3/8 inch long, they are ready.
Process the chickpeas and sweet potato in a food processor until you have a fairly smooth but lightly textured mix.

Add the flaxseed, tahini, cumin seeds, chile, ginger, and coconut aminos sauce to the processor and blend to combine. Transfer the mixture to a bowl and stir in the parsley and cilantro. Season with salt and pepper, if using.

Mold the mixture into 25 small balls and roll them in the sesame seeds. Transfer to a nonstick dehydrator sheet on a dehydrator tray. (If using the oven, use a nonstick oven pan.) Dehydrate on low (115°F) for 6 hours, then turn them over and dehydrate on low for an additional 2 hours.
To make the salad, mix the vegetables together in a serving bowl and drizzle with the olive oil.
To make the hummus, put all the ingredients into a clean processor and blend until you have a fairly smooth mix. Serve the falafels alongside the dip and the salad.

notes: The chickpeas need three to five days to sprout and the falafel eight hours to dehydrate. Sprouted chickpeas are not recommended for young children, older adults, pregnant women, or anyone with a weakened immune system.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings (20 balls) to 5 servings (25 balls), the VegBatch standard.
Renamed to flag that the falafel is raw as well as the hummus.

title: Zucchini Spaghetti with Garlic Cream Sauce
original_title: Spaghetti with Garlic Cream Sauce and Baby Tomatoes
description: Spiralized zucchini tossed in olive oil and salt, topped with a thick sauce of soaked almonds, garlic, scallion and cider vinegar, and finished with sun-dried tomatoes, baby plum tomatoes and basil.
keeps_note: The recipe says serve immediately — spiralized zucchini turns to water within hours.

ingredients.raw_text: 2 1/2 tablespoons cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil
1 2/3 cups raw skinned almonds, soaked in water for 2 hours, drained and rinsed
ingredients.prep_note: raw skinned, soaked 2 hours, drained and rinsed

instructions.text: To make the garlic cream sauce, pulse the soaked almonds in a food processor until they are ground. Add the almond milk, garlic, scallion, vinegar, and salt, then blend until you have a thick, creamy paste. Transfer to a bowl.
Toss the zucchini spirals in the olive oil and salt. Divide the spirals between five serving bowls.
Spoon the creamy sauce into the center of each bowl, then top with the sun-dried tomatoes, plum tomatoes, scallions, and basil leaves. Serve immediately.

notes: The almonds need 2 hours of soaking. Summer squash works in summer and butternut squash in winter.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 2 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.
Renamed to say the spaghetti is zucchini — there is no pasta in it.

title: Gado Gado Salad
description: Raw cauliflower, broccoli, savoy cabbage, bean sprouts, cucumber and red pepper tossed in an Indonesian peanut and soy dressing warmed just enough to bring it together.
keeps_note: The vegetables are sturdy and the dressing keeps — hold them apart and toss as you serve.

ingredients.raw_text: 1/3 head cauliflower, cored and cut into small florets
ingredients.prep_note: cored and cut into small florets

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 cucumbers, peeled, halved lengthwise, seeded, and thickly sliced
ingredients.prep_note: peeled, halved lengthwise, seeded, and thickly sliced

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/4 red bell peppers, halved, seeded, and finely chopped

ingredients.estimate_basis: a lime yields about 2 tablespoons

instructions.text: Put the cauliflower, broccoli, cabbage, bean sprouts, cucumber, and red bell pepper into a salad bowl and toss gently together.

To make the dressing, warm 1 tablespoon of the oil in a pan over medium heat. (You can warm raw food below a temperature of 104°F.) Add the peanuts and garlic and warm for 2 to 3 minutes, then remove from the heat and stir in the soy sauce, lime juice, chile, and remaining oil. Leave at room temperature for a couple of hours.
When ready to eat, mix the dressing thoroughly, spoon the dressing over the salad and toss them gently together. Spoon into five bowls, then serve immediately.

notes: The dressing rests a couple of hours at room temperature before it goes on. Mung bean sprouts are the easiest to find and work well here.
household_edits: Scaled from the book's 4 servings to 5, the VegBatch standard.

title: Peach and Orange Granita
description: Peaches blended whole with orange and lime juice, agave and vanilla, then frozen and forked through in stages so it sets in crystals rather than a block.
keeps_note: It lives in the freezer — fork it through again before serving.

ingredients.estimate_basis: a large orange yields about 1/4 cup of juice
a lime yields about 2 tablespoons
half a bean yields about 1/2 teaspoon of seeds

ingredients.raw_text: 1 orange, cut into slices, to decorate

instructions.text: Put the orange juice, peaches, lime juice, agave nectar, and vanilla seeds into a blender and blend until smooth, or until a few small peach pieces are left.
Pour the mixture into a shallow, freeze-proof container, cover with a lid, and freeze for 2 hours.
Stir the mixture with a fork, bringing the frozen edges into the center. Replace the lid and freeze for another 2 hours.
Stir again and freeze for another hour, or until nearly frozen in the center. Stir again before dividing the granita among four glasses. Serve decorated with the orange slices and mint leaves.

notes: About five hours in the freezer with three stirs. One large mango, two papayas or four nectarines work in place of the peaches.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 4 servings — a dessert.

title: Mixed Fruit Soup Bowl
description: Two chilled fruit purees — papaya with strawberry, and honeydew melon with mint and preserved ginger — swirled together in the bowl and scattered with diced fruit and blueberries.
keeps_note: The two purees keep a couple of days chilled; swirl and garnish as you serve.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 honeydew melon, seeded, peeled, and chopped

instructions.text: Reserving 1 tablespoon of the chopped papaya, put the remainder into a food processor with 1 3/4 cups of the strawberries and process to a smooth puree.
Pour into a small bowl and chill in the refrigerator for 10 minutes.

Put all but 1 tablespoon of the chopped melon into the food processor with half the mint leaves, the ginger syrup, and preserved ginger. Process to a smooth puree. Pour into a small bowl and chill in the refrigerator for 10 minutes.
When you are ready to serve, divide each soup among four bowls, then use a knife to swirl them together. Drop a couple of ice cubes into each bowl.
Dice the reserved fruits and sprinkle them over the soup, together with the blueberries and remaining mint leaves.

notes: Raspberries work in place of the strawberries. Use whatever fruit is actually in season.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 4 servings — a dessert.

title: Cacao and Avocado Mousse with Cinnamon Berries
original_title: Cacao and Avocado Mousse with Cinnamon Berries
description: Mashed avocado blended with cacao powder, agave, vanilla and a little chili powder into a dense chocolate mousse, chilled in ramekins and topped with strawberries, raspberries and cinnamon.
keeps_note: Chills at least 4 hours and holds in the ramekins; add the berries as you serve.

ingredients.estimate_basis: half a bean yields about 1/2 teaspoon of seeds

ingredients.raw_text: 1/3 cup hulled wild strawberries or hulled small strawberries

instructions.text: Scoop the avocado flesh into a large bowl and mash lightly with a fork. Stir in the cacao powder, agave nectar, vanilla seeds, and chili powder. Blend thoroughly with an immersion blender until the mixture is thick and smooth. Stir in the coconut milk and blend again.
Spoon the avocado mixture into ramekins (individual ceramic dishes) or small, stemmed glasses. Cover with plastic wrap and chill for at least 4 hours.
Decorate the avocado mousses evenly with the berries and sprinkle the cinnamon over each dish. Serve immediately.

notes: Four hours of chilling. The chili powder is not a mistake — it lifts the cacao rather than making it hot.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 4 servings — a dessert.

title: Layered Raw Apple Pie
description: A pressed walnut and date crust frozen firm, filled with a spiced date, banana and apple puree layered with thinly sliced apple and golden raisins, and dusted with cinnamon. Nothing is baked.
keeps_note: Chills firm and holds in the refrigerator — a whole pie for the week.

ingredients.raw_text: 2 tablespoons melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil
8 Medjool dates, pitted, soaked in water for 4 hours, drained, and rinsed
ingredients.prep_note: pitted, soaked 4 hours, drained, and rinsed

ingredients.raw_text: 1 small banana, peeled and coarsely chopped
1 apple, such as Red Delicious, Pink Lady, or Fuji, peeled, cored and coarsely chopped

ingredients.estimate_basis: half a lemon yields about 1 1/2 tablespoons

ingredients.raw_text: 5 sweet, crisp apples, such as Red Delicious, Pink Lady, or Fuji, cored

instructions.text: Line an 8 x 2 1/2-inch round cake pan with nonstick parchment paper. Set aside.
To make the pie crust, pulse the walnuts in a food processor for a few seconds, then add the dates and process again until you have a fine, sticky mixture. Add the coconut oil and blend again.
Spoon the mixture into the prepared pan. Press down thoroughly and evenly, and put into the freezer to set for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.

To make the filling, put the soaked dates, banana, and chopped apple into a clean food processor with the cinnamon, nutmeg, vanilla seeds, and salt. Pulse to thoroughly combine, then spoon into a mixing bowl.

Stir the lemon juice into a bowl of cold water. Using a mandoline slicer or sharp knife, thinly slice the dessert apples, adding them to the water bowl as you work — the acid from the lemon stops them from turning brown.

Spoon a thin layer of the filling onto the chilled pie crust and top with a few of the golden raisins and a layer of sliced apples. Push the apple slices down well. Repeat until you have used all the filling, sliced apples, and golden raisins, then dust the top of the pie with the cinnamon. Chill in the refrigerator for an hour before serving.

notes: The dates soak 4 hours, the crust freezes 2 hours and the finished pie chills an hour. Firm dessert pears such as Bartlett work in place of the apples.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 8 servings — a whole pie.
Renamed to flag that it is raw.

title: Raw Banana, Pineapple, and Peanut Pie
original_title: Raw Banana, Pineapple, and Peanut Pie
description: A frozen crust of hazelnuts, Brazil nuts and pecans bound with dates and maple syrup, filled with blended banana, peanut butter, pineapple and creamed coconut, topped with soaked banana slices and pecan halves.
keeps_note: Freezes firm and lives in the refrigerator until served.

ingredients.raw_text: 2 tablespoons melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil
1 1/2 tablespoons melted raw unsweetened creamed coconut
1 banana, sliced and soaked in 1/4 cup pineapple juice for 30 minutes
ingredients.prep_note: sliced and soaked in 1/4 cup pineapple juice for 30 minutes

ingredients.raw_text: 2 thin slices pineapple, chopped, to decorate

instructions.text: Line an 8 x 2 1/2-inch round cake pan with nonstick parchment paper. Set aside.
To make the pie crust, put all the nuts into a food processor and pulse for a few seconds. Add the dates, maple syrup, coconut oil, and water. Process until you have a crumbly, fairly fine mixture.
Press the nut mixture evenly and firmly into the prepared pan. Chill in the freezer for 2 hours.

Meanwhile, make the filling. Put all the ingredients into a food processor and process until the mixture is thoroughly blended. Spoon the filling onto the frozen crust and smooth the top. Freeze again for an hour, or until the filling is firm.
To make the topping, arrange the soaked banana slices over the pie with the pineapple pieces and pecan halves. Keep the pie in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

notes: Three hours in the freezer across two stages. Grate raw cacao nibs over the top just before serving.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 8 servings — a whole pie.
The pineapple juice the banana soaks in was listed only inside the topping line; it is broken out as its own ingredient so it reaches the shopping list.

title: Chocolate-Avocado Lime Pie
description: A macadamia, pecan and Brazil nut crust under a cashew, coconut and avocado lime filling, finished with a cashew and cacao chocolate topping and fresh coconut shavings.
keeps_note: Sets firm in the refrigerator and keeps several days.

ingredients.raw_text: 5 Medjool dates, pitted and coarsely chopped
1 tablespoon melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil
1 1/2 cups raw cashew nuts, soaked in water for 4 hours, drained, and rinsed
1 3/4 cups shredded fresh white coconut meat
2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons melted raw unsweetened creamed coconut
2 ripe avocados, peeled, pitted, and coarsely chopped
ingredients.prep_note: ripe, peeled, pitted, and coarsely chopped

ingredients.estimate_basis: a lime yields about 2 tablespoons

ingredients.raw_text: 1 tablespoon melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil
1 tablespoon melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil
1/4 cup melted raw unsweetened creamed coconut
1/3 cup fresh white coconut meat shavings, to decorate

instructions.text: Line an 8-inch round cake pan with nonstick parchment paper and set aside.
Put the dates into a small bowl and soak for 10 minutes in enough warm water to cover. Drain and reserve the soaking water.

To make the pie crust, pulse the macadamia nuts, pecans, and Brazil nuts in a food processor for 10 seconds, then add the soaked dates and pulse again until everything is finely chopped. Add the agave nectar, soaking water, and coconut oil, then pulse again.
Press the mixture into the prepared pan and chill in the refrigerator for 2 hours, until firm.

To make the avocado filling, pulse the soaked cashew nuts in a clean food processor until you have a creamy puree. Transfer to a mixing bowl. Process the coconut meat to a paste, adding as little of the creamed coconut as necessary. Add the coconut to the mixing bowl.

Add the avocados to the processor with the lime juice, and pulse to a puree. Transfer to the mixing bowl. Stir in the rest of the creamed coconut, the coconut oil, and the agave nectar. Combine everything thoroughly.
Spread the filling over the firm crust and smooth the top. Chill in the refrigerator for another 2 hours.
Meanwhile, make the chocolate topping. Cream the cashew nuts as before and transfer to a small mixing bowl. Stir in the rest of the ingredients, reserving the coconut shavings for decoration.
When the filling is cool and firm, spread or pipe the topping over the pie. Decorate with the coconut shavings and chill until ready to serve.

notes: The cashews soak 4 hours and the pie chills in two 2-hour stages, so allow most of a day.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 8 servings — a whole pie.

title: Fig and Almond Cream Squares
description: A frozen base of sun-dried figs, dates, walnuts and Brazil nuts under a soaked-almond cream enriched with coconut flour and vanilla, folded through with fresh fig, cut into squares and topped with fig slices.
keeps_note: Frozen firm and served chilled — cut squares keep several days.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 1/2 teaspoons melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil
1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon raw almonds, soaked in water for 4 hours, drained, and rinsed
1 tablespoon melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil

instructions.text: Line a 7-inch baking pan with nonstick parchment paper and set aside.

Put the sun-dried figs, dates, nuts, flaxseed, and coconut oil into a food processor and pulse until you have a crumbly, sticky mixture. Press into the prepared pan and freeze for 1 to 2 hours, until firm.

To make the topping, rub the skins off the soaked almonds — they should come away easily — and put them into a clean food processor, reserving five almonds for decoration. Pulse until you have a thick, creamy puree, then add the almond milk, coconut flour, agave nectar, vanilla seeds, and coconut oil. Blend again.
Scoop the flesh out of the five fresh figs and mash them with a fork in a small bowl. Stir them into the topping mixture.

Smooth the topping over the frozen mixture and freeze again for 1 to 2 hours. When firm, cut into squares and top each square with a slice of fresh fig. Chop the five reserved almonds and put a little on each fig slice. Serve the squares chilled.

notes: The almonds soak 4 hours and the squares freeze in two stages. Cut each square into four small bites to serve as party snacks.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 9 squares — a batch.
Renamed from "Creamy Fig Squares" to name the almond cream.

title: Almond and Berry Energy Bars
description: Dehydrated bars of ground soaked almonds, pumpkin and sunflower seeds, goji berries, cacao nibs and goldenberries bound with agave and creamed coconut, coated in a cashew and cacao chocolate topping.
keeps_note: Dehydrated and chocolate-coated — these are built to sit in the refrigerator.

ingredients.raw_text: 3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons raw almonds, soaked in water for 4 hours, drained, and rinsed
1/3 cup dried goji berries, soaked in water for 30 minutes, drained, and rinsed
1/2 cup raw cashew nuts, soaked in water for 4 hours, drained, and rinsed
2 tablespoons melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil
2 tablespoons melted raw unsweetened creamed coconut

instructions.text: You will need a dehydrator for this recipe. If you don't have one, an electric oven may have a setting low enough — the defrost setting or slightly higher, or a designated dehydrate setting. Check the temperature with an oven thermometer before dehydrating in a standard oven.
Soak two-thirds of the pumpkin and sunflower seeds in water for 4 hours. Drain and rinse.
Line an 8-inch shallow container with nonstick parchment paper. (If using the oven, line an oven pan with parchment paper.) Set aside.
Grind the soaked almonds and seeds in a food processor. Add the flaxseed, agave nectar, and cinnamon to the processor and pulse until well combined. Transfer the mixture to a mixing bowl.
Add the rest of the seeds to the bowl with the soaked goji berries, cacao nibs, goldenberries, sesame seeds, buckwheat flour, and creamed coconut. Stir well.
Press the mixture into the prepared container and dehydrate on high (140°F) for an hour, then on low (115°F) for 3 hours.

Remove the mixture from the pan and cut into 10 bars. Line a dehydrator tray with a nonstick dehydrator sheet. (If using the oven, use a parchment-lined oven pan.) Transfer the bars to the sheet and dehydrate again on low until they are dry on the outside but still a little soft on the inside.
Meanwhile, make the topping. Pulse the soaked cashew nuts in a clean food processor until smooth and creamy. Spoon into a mixing bowl, add the rest of the ingredients, and mix well with a fork.
When the bars are completely cool, coat them with the chocolate topping and chill in the refrigerator until set.

notes: Four hours of soaking and several hours of dehydrating across two stages.
household_edits: Raw honey swapped for raw agave nectar in the chocolate topping so the recipe is vegan.
Kept at the book's 10 bars — a batch.
Renamed from "Almond and Berry Pick-Me-Up Bars".

title: Cashew Cookies
description: Soaked cashews blended to a butter and worked into coconut flour with coconut milk, agave and vanilla, rolled into balls, forked flat and dehydrated until crisp outside and soft in the middle.
keeps_note: Stored in the refrigerator — a batch lasts the week.

ingredients.raw_text: 3/4 cup raw cashew nuts, soaked in water for 4 hours, drained, and rinsed
3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons raw coconut flour, plus 1 tablespoon for dusting

instructions.text: You will need a dehydrator for this recipe. If you don't have one, an electric oven may have a setting low enough — the defrost setting or slightly higher, or a designated dehydrate setting. Check the temperature with an oven thermometer before dehydrating in a standard oven.
Pulse the soaked cashew nuts in a food processor until you have a smooth nut butter.
Sift the coconut flour into a mixing bowl and stir in the cashew butter along with the remaining ingredients. Mix well with a fork until you have a soft dough.

Cover the dough and chill in the refrigerator for 2 hours. Meanwhile, line a dehydrator tray with a nonstick dehydrator sheet and set aside. (If using the oven, line an oven pan with parchment paper.)

Roll the chilled dough into 16 small balls, using your hands. Place them on the prepared sheet and flatten a little. (If using the oven, add the balls to your oven pan lined with parchment paper.) Using a fork, make a row of lines over the surface of each cookie. Dust with a sifted tablespoon of coconut flour.
Dehydrate the cookies on low (115°F) for about 10 hours, or until they are lightly crisp on the outside but still a little soft in the center. Store in the refrigerator.

notes: Four hours of soaking, two of chilling and about ten of dehydrating — start these a day ahead. Almond flour and almond butter give a different flavour.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 16 cookies — a batch.

title: No-Bake Carrot Cake
description: Carrots and fresh coconut processed with dried apricots, walnuts and Medjool dates, bound with buckwheat and coconut flour and orange juice, layered in the pan with a soaked cashew cream and frozen rather than baked.
keeps_note: Frozen in layers and served chilled — keeps well.

ingredients.raw_text: 2/3 cup coarsely chopped fresh coconut white meat
1/3 cup plus 2 tablespoons raw coconut flour
1 1/2 cups raw cashew nuts, soaked in water for 4 hours, drained, and rinsed
2 1/2 tablespoons melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil

instructions.text: Line a 7-inch round cake pan with nonstick parchment paper and set aside.

To make the cashew cream, blend the soaked nuts with half the orange juice in a food processor until creamy, then add the remaining ingredients and process until smooth. Transfer the cream to a bowl and keep in the refrigerator.
For the cake, pulse the carrots and coconut in a food processor for a few seconds, then add the apricots, half the walnuts, and half the dates. Process until everything is finely chopped.

Transfer the cake batter to a large mixing bowl. Coarsely chop the remaining walnuts and dates, and add to the bowl. In a separate bowl, combine the flours, cinnamon, and salt, then add to the cake batter and combine thoroughly until all the flour is incorporated. Add the orange juice and stir well.
Spoon half the cake batter evenly into the prepared pan. Top with half the cashew cream and smooth the top. Freeze for 2 hours.
Remove the cake from the freezer and spoon the rest of the cake batter over the cream. Top with the remaining cream. Freeze for an additional hour, then decorate with the walnut halves.

notes: Four hours of soaking and three of freezing across two stages. Sun-dried apricot or mango pieces work in place of the walnut halves on top.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 8 servings — a whole cake.

title: Almond and Pistachio Brownies
description: Ground almonds and pistachios pulsed with cacao powder, Medjool dates and vanilla into a dense no-bake brownie studded with cacao nibs, under a cacao and almond milk topping.
keeps_note: Cut and stored in the refrigerator — a batch keeps well.

ingredients.raw_text: 2 tablespoons melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil
1 tablespoon chopped raw pistachio nuts, to decorate

instructions.text: Line an 8-inch square baking pan with nonstick parchment paper and set aside.

Reserve 3 tablespoons of the almonds and 2 1/2 tablespoons of the pistachio nuts. Pulse the remaining nuts in a food processor until you have fairly fine crumbs. Add the cacao powder, dates, vanilla seeds, and salt, and pulse again to form a thick mixture.
Transfer the brownie mixture to a bowl and stir in the reserved nuts and the cacao nibs. Press it evenly into the prepared pan.

To make the topping, blend the cacao powder, agave nectar, coconut oil, and vanilla seeds in a blender with enough of the almond milk to make a fairly thick sauce. Pour the sauce over the brownie mixture and sprinkle with the pistachio nuts. Chill in the refrigerator for an hour, or until the topping is set.
Cut the brownie into 16 squares and store in the refrigerator.

notes: An hour of chilling and no oven. Walnuts and pecans work in place of the almonds and pistachios.
household_edits: Raw honey swapped for raw agave nectar in the topping so the recipe is vegan.
Kept at the book's 16 brownies — a batch.

title: No-Bake Almond Melts
description: Fifteen small chilled balls of ground almonds and coconut flour bound with agave and coconut oil, in three flavours — lemon rolled in grated coconut, pistachio rolled in ground pistachio, and mango dusted with coconut flour.
keeps_note: Chilled and firm — keeps several days in the refrigerator.

ingredients.raw_text: 1 tablespoon melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil
1 1/2 tablespoons melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil
2 tablespoons raw coconut flour, plus 1 tablespoon for dusting
1 1/2 teaspoons melted cold-pressed extra virgin coconut oil

instructions.text: To make the lemon melts, combine all the ingredients except the grated coconut in a small mixing bowl. Using your hands, form the mixture into five balls and roll them in the coconut. Transfer to a plate and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.

To make the pistachio melts, grind the pistachio nuts in a processor. Set aside 2 tablespoons of the ground pistachio nuts and add the rest to a small mixing bowl with the remaining ingredients. Mix thoroughly, then form the mixture into five balls and roll them in the remaining ground pistachio nuts. Transfer to a plate and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.

To make the mango melts, combine all the ingredients except 1 tablespoon of the coconut flour in a small mixing bowl, then form the mixture into five balls. Sift the remaining coconut flour over them. Transfer to a plate and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Take the melts out of the refrigerator about 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Three separate mixtures of five balls each, all chilled 30 minutes. For papaya melts, use 1/3 cup plus 1 1/2 tablespoons ground almonds, 2 tablespoons ripe papaya flesh, 1 1/2 teaspoons melted coconut oil and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla bean seeds, rolled in 2 tablespoons grated fresh coconut.
household_edits: Kept at the book's 15 melts — a batch.
Renamed from "Pastel Melts" — the colours are incidental and the name said nothing about the food.
